summary: On 12 June 2025 a policy change with blank fields reached Google's Service Control binaries, which had a new, unprotected feature. A null pointer put them into a crash loop worldwide and APIs returned 503 errors for hours.

overview.background: Service Control checks policy and quota for API requests across Google Cloud. Its policy data is stored in regional Spanner tables that replicate globally within seconds.
systems: Google Cloud APIs and Google Workspace products
overview.impact: Google Cloud and Workspace products returned 503 errors in many regions from about 10:51 AM PDT. Most products recovered by about 1:45 PM, us-central1 later, and Vertex AI Online Prediction fully at 6:18 PM.
overview.severity: A global, multi-product outage of several hours. Google gives no formal severity.
overview.gaps: Some times in the page differ (incident end 13:49 in the mini report, 18:18 in the status header).

timeline.e: A new Service Control feature for quota policy checks is released without a feature flag.
A policy change with blank fields is inserted into regional Spanner tables and replicates globally within seconds.
The incident starts: Service Control binaries crash on the blank fields.
First public post acknowledges issues with multiple Google Cloud products.
The root cause is identified and mitigations are applied.
All regions except us-central1 are mitigated.
Most Google Cloud products are fully recovered.
Mitigation is applied in us-central1 and multi-region US.
Vertex AI Online Prediction is fully recovered.

rootCause.trigger: A policy change containing blank fields was written to the regional Spanner tables.
rootCause.underlying: A new feature added on 29 May had no error handling and no feature flag, so the blank fields caused a null pointer and a crash loop in every region.
contributing: Policy data replicates globally within seconds
The binary crashed instead of failing open
In large regions restarting tasks overloaded Spanner because there was no randomized exponential backoff
Customer monitoring and Google's status page were also affected

evidence.label: What was missing
evidence.body: The issue with this change was that it did not have appropriate error handling nor was it feature flag protected.

evidence.label: Why it spread
evidence.body: This occurred globally given each regional deployment.

evidence.label: A simulated guard
evidence.note: Shows fail-open handling with a last known good value. Not Google code.

diagnose.step: Find the first change near the start time.
diagnose.why: A policy insertion at about 10:45 matched.

diagnose.step: Check whether the binary crashes on specific data.
diagnose.why: The crash was in a null-pointer path.

diagnose.step: Look at database load during restarts.
diagnose.why: us-central1 was slow because of the restart stampede.

correct.why: Google froze all Service Control changes.

correct.step: Bypass the faulty check and throttle task creation.
Route to multi-regional databases where needed.

verify.why: Dataflow and Vertex AI took longer.

prevent.step: Gate every new code path behind a feature flag.
Validate and stage globally replicated data.

fix.safety: Bypassing a quota check changes who can call what. Re-enable it as soon as the data is fixed.

troubleshoot.scenario: A control-plane binary crashes on startup everywhere and APIs return 503. A policy table changed 5 minutes before.
clues: A new feature shipped two weeks ago
troubleshoot.question: What are your first three actions?
troubleshoot.answer: Freeze policy pushes, bypass the faulty check or roll back the data, throttle restarts with jitter, and route to healthy databases. Then fix the null handling.

options: Blank fields in policy data hitting an unprotected feature
rootcause.why: Google names blank fields and a null pointer.

remediation.answer: No new code path on a critical binary ships without a flag that can disable it remotely.
Reject policy records with missing required fields before they replicate.
Exponential backoff with full jitter on restarts and database retries.

design.prompt: Design a global policy system that cannot be crashed by a bad record.
design.answer: Validate at write, replicate in stages with bake time, make consumers fail open with last known good, and rate limit restarts.

checks.q: When was the new feature released?

checks.why: Restart load overloaded the Spanner table there.

options: Service Control changes and manual policy pushes

checks.q: What would have limited the blast radius?
checks.why: Google says the change lacked flag protection.

practices: Fail open with last known good
